notes: Both address experimental design choices regarding landmarks and ecological validity (9 shared claims, 0.6 Jaccard). LLM finds the design well-justified with validation data confirming sufficient visual flow. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about generalizability to real driving, requesting discussion of how impoverished stimuli might affect results compared to real scenarios.

Both agree the anti-fog manipulation provides strong confirmatory evidence (5 shared claims, 0.312 Jaccard). LLM notes robust statistical support and predicted reversal of perceptual bias. Peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of the manuscript's important contribution without specific challenges.

Both support the perception-behavior link (4 shared claims, 0.286 Jaccard). LLM emphasizes strong statistical effects and consistent relationship across experiments. Peer reviewers implicitly accepted this pattern as part of the manuscript's contribution, focusing on methodological details rather than challenging the core finding.

Both support core findings about speed underestimation with uniform contrast (4 shared claims, 0.222 Jaccard). LLM cites strong statistical evidence validating the experimental paradigm. Peer reviewers accepted the main experimental results, requesting only methodological clarifications rather than challenging the findings.

Partial overlap on speed overestimation in fog (2 shared claims: C24, C4). LLM emphasizes robust demonstration across experiments as primary contribution. Peer review R1 addresses broader core findings including this result. Both support the finding, though peer review groups it with additional claims not in LLM R2.

Partial overlap on spatial distribution mechanism (4 shared claims, 0.19 Jaccard). LLM supports the claim that spatial distribution rather than global contrast determines speed perception. Peer review R1 accepts core findings including this mechanism. Both support, though they group claims differently.

Both address statistical evidence for speed underestimation (4 shared claims, 0.2 Jaccard). LLM finds strong statistical support validating findings. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about statistical presentation clarity, noting missing ANOVA details and unspecified error bars, requiring clarification rather than questioning the underlying data.

Both address discrimination sensitivity (JND) effects (3 shared claims, 0.158 Jaccard). LLM finds statistically significant differential effects with ecological explanation. Peer reviewers express uncertainty due to insufficient transparency in statistical presentation, requesting clearer analysis details and specification of which differences were significant.

Partial overlap on behavioral consequences (5 shared claims, 0.217 Jaccard). LLM emphasizes strong statistical effects demonstrating perception-action link. Peer review R1 accepts core findings including behavioral results. Both support, though LLM R3 includes additional claims about behavioral experiments not specifically addressed in peer R1.

Both address behavioral consequences with partial overlap (4 shared claims, 0.154 Jaccard). LLM finds convincing demonstration with strong statistical effects. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about statistical presentation clarity, requesting better specification of analyses and significant differences, though not challenging the underlying findings.

Both address anti-fog manipulation with partial overlap (4 shared claims, 0.148 Jaccard). LLM finds strong confirmatory evidence with robust statistical support. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about statistical presentation transparency, requesting clearer analysis details, though the anti-fog findings themselves were not specifically challenged.

Minimal overlap on fog effects (2 shared claims: C64, C85). LLM emphasizes speed overestimation in fog as primary contribution. Peer R5 addresses anti-fog manipulation specifically. Both support fog-related findings, but address different aspects with limited claim overlap.

LLM addresses theoretical gap in Bayesian and ratio models (C128-C130). No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses these theoretical claims. LLM finds the identification of model limitations well-justified, but peer reviewers did not explicitly evaluate this theoretical contribution.

Peer reviewers question whether haptic feedback from steering wheel was adequately controlled (C145), expressing uncertainty about potential confounds. No corresponding LLM result specifically addresses this methodological concern about haptic feedback as a potential speed cue.

Peer reviewers raise concerns about contrast adaptation effects from prolonged experimental sessions and potential sequence effects over trials. No corresponding LLM result specifically addresses these temporal confound concerns, which peer reviewers found inadequately discussed.
